title: Emil Stein and Happy Bolton, New Orleans theater drummers
summary: They discuss Stein's drum set-up and Happy Bolton, who played drums and xylophone in the theater.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Say, something I wanted to get. What was that, Stan's, the drummer's name that you talked about?
Yeah. He worked in that band in the palace, the Santo. That's where Santo started.
And some other, uh, drummer, they used to tell me about, I don't know his name, played vaudeville here. Do you remember anybody sensational that you can think of?
Well, Stein was the only, he was the only one. He was the only one. He was the only one.
He was the only one that, that, that, that ever attempted to play jazz. Huh?
What did Happy play like? Drums?

Oh man, Happy was, Happy was a player. Happy played drums and, and, and, and solophones. He played on the boat with, with Faith and him. He played the Lyric Theater. They used to have a, Lyric Theater right on the corner of Burgundy and, and Aberdeen. Well, they used to bring acts in like, like reviews, colored reviews, you know, like Ethel Wallace. She, she's the one that took, uh, what's called them away from here, that, uh, had a guy around here by the name of Jackson. Willie Jackson. Oh yeah. She took them away with me and brought them to New York, made an MC out of him. And, uh, well they used to bring some fine acts down there.
What if I asked the Monk, well who did he play with?
